$comment: Refusals the playback compiler raises against constructs a user can author. An entry records who owns the refusal and why it stands; it is not a claim that the refusal is correct. status=live-defect means the document is authorable today and unplayable, and the refusal is a placeholder for work that has not happened; status=intended means the refusal is the answer. Enforced by tools/scripts/negative_capability_check.py.

refusals.reason: set_track_device_chain authors processing on a track that a SequenceRef then nests. A device is bound to the track it processes, and flattening dissolves the child track entirely: its clips become leaves on the parent, whose own chain already serves every other clip there. Running the child's devices over the parent would process unrelated material, and dropping them plays the child dry, so the compile refuses and names the track. This was one half of the former NestedSequenceUnsupported umbrella, split so the refusal says which construct is missing. Flip this to intended, or retire it, when a flattened group can keep its own processing: a sub-bus or nested-track-bus construct that survives flattening is the missing piece and its arrival is the checkable condition.

set_track_automation_lane authors a curve on a track that a SequenceRef then nests. A lane is a value over the child track's own timeline, and the flattened leaf has nowhere to hold a curve: ClipPlaybackProperties::gain_linear in core/timeline/include/pulp/timeline/clip.hpp is a scalar, so even the one lane whose destination exists has no time-varying sink and would have to freeze at a single point. This was the other half of the former NestedSequenceUnsupported umbrella. The gain-on-media sub-case is genuine pending work and its checkable condition is a per-clip automation sink, an envelope field a renderer reads. The pan and MIDI-gain sub-cases are not waiting on that: pan has no per-clip destination at any level, for the reason NestedMixerPanUnsupported states, and no renderer scales an event by clip gain, for the reason NestedGainSinkUnsupported states, so those two can only ever be closed by declaring them intended rather than by lifting the refusal.

A leaf clip inside a nested sequence is absolute-anchored while the SequenceRef placement reaching it is musical. Flattening must place that leaf on the owner's musical timeline, but an absolute clip's position is defined in samples and is meant to stay fixed as tempo moves, so the flattened result would have to be musical and absolute at once and the lowered program has no such hybrid domain. Refusing names the clip rather than silently re-anchoring it and moving the author's audio under a tempo change. Note this refusal is reachable, unlike the sibling guard on the placement itself: Clip::create_absolute rejects SequenceRef content, so a placement carrying a reference is always musical and its guard is a defensive backstop raising InvalidStructure. Lifting this one needs a product decision about whether nesting re-anchors an absolute leaf or preserves it, and only then a lowered representation that can carry the answer; it may legitimately end as intended.

set_track_mixer authors a stereo balance on a track that a SequenceRef then nests. Flattening folds the child into the parent track, a clip carries no pan of its own, and the parent's single pan also serves every other clip on that track, so the child's balance can be neither written anywhere nor dropped without silently centring the child. Unlike gain there is no sink for any content kind. The refusal is the answer rather than a placeholder: declining to flatten is correct while a flattened leaf has nowhere to carry its own stereo placement. Flip this back to live-defect when ClipPlaybackProperties in core/timeline/include/pulp/timeline/clip.hpp gains a pan or balance field, because that field is the missing sink and its arrival is the checkable condition.

A nested gain composes by multiplying into the flattened leaf's clip gain, which only reaches a renderer for media content; note, registered and opaque leaves compile to events and no renderer scales an event by the gain of the clip that carried it. Folding a child fader into one would discard it with nothing to read the loss from, so the compile refuses and names the leaf. The refusal is the answer rather than a placeholder: what a clip gain should mean for an event is a product question about velocity versus level, not a lowering detail. Flip this back to live-defect when a MIDI or registered leaf gains a defined output-gain sink, an event renderer that reads ClipPlaybackProperties::gain_linear, because that sink is the checkable condition.

set_clip_playback_properties authors a fade on the SequenceRef placement itself. That fade now composes: the ramp travels beside each flattened leaf in owner-timeline ticks as a window of fade progress, the renderer reads the leaf's position within it, and nesting one level deeper appends another ramp rather than folding two into one. What remains refused is the same sink question NestedGainSinkUnsupported asks about a static gain. A fade is a time-varying gain, and note, registered and opaque leaves compile to events that no renderer scales by the gain of the clip that carried them, so a fade over one of those leaves would have nowhere to land; the refusal names the leaf instead of playing it at full level through an envelope the author wrote. It is scoped to the leaves a ramp actually reaches — a leaf lying wholly past a ramp reads unity and does not refuse. The refusal is the answer rather than a placeholder, for the reason the gain case gives: what a clip gain should mean for an event is a product question about velocity versus level, not a lowering detail. Flip this back to live-defect when a MIDI or registered leaf gains a defined output-gain sink, an event renderer that reads ClipPlaybackProperties::gain_linear, because that sink is the checkable condition and it is the same one the gain refusal waits on.

set_track_freeze seals a rendered artifact over a track and a SequenceRef then nests that track. Freeze is a substitution: SequenceContentLowerer::begin_track returns Freeze content and discards the arrangement, so the artifact is what a top-level frozen track plays. The nested walk descends into the child's clips and has no substitution step, so it would play the arrangement the author froze — quietly undoing the freeze rather than failing. Refusing names the track instead. Flip this to intended, or retire it, when a flattened leaf can carry rendered media standing in for a whole child track: a LoweredClip content kind that holds a TrackFreeze artifact is the missing construct and its arrival is the checkable condition.

set_active_take_lane selects a comp lane on a track a SequenceRef then nests. Selection is the same substitution freeze performs: begin_track returns ActiveTake content built from the lane's comp segments and discards the arrangement. The nested walk reads the arrangement, so honouring the nesting would sound exactly the material the author deselected. The refusal is scoped to a SELECTED lane; an unselected lane is inert at both levels and does not refuse. Flip this when a flattened leaf can carry comped take segments, the same missing construct freeze needs.

The document model lets a device be placed post-fader, but the binding wires the whole device chain ahead of the track's mixer node and the mixer exposes no post-gain insertion tap, so a post-fader placement has nowhere to run; the refusal stands until the mixer publishes that tap.

Narrowed rather than deleted now that the event domain is admitted: an audio-to-audio insert is still refused because no built-in occupies that slot and the binding has no audio-in device node to wire, and a placement whose declared slot kind disagrees with its binding key's catalog domain is refused because the declaration, not the key, decides where the node is wired.

An external, generated, or unresolved device is the caller's to build; the chain-level filter already hands such a chain back before this per-placement guard can fire, so it is a defensive restatement of the built-in-only contract rather than a refusal a document reaches today.

A binding key outside the built-in device catalog names no device at all: there is no descriptor to size the node, no factory to build it, and no latency to compensate, so admitting it would bind an empty node into the chain and call it playable.

The chain's event-compensation shift is resolved once at prepare and cached for the audio thread; a bypassed device still reports its look-ahead latency, so admitting bypass would either schedule against a shift the bypassed chain no longer imposes or require the shift to move under automation, which the cached prepared number cannot follow.

A wet/dry mix other than fully wet has no meaning in the event domain — there is no dry event stream to blend and no audio to crossfade at the instrument, which produces sound from nothing — so the refusal stands until a per-domain mix contract defines what blending an event stream means.

A placement carrying a state reference asks the binding to restore device state the built-in slots have no deserialisation path for; admitting it would silently drop the authored state and play a differently configured device than the document describes.

A track offering live input into a chain compensated by reading ahead would diverge from its scheduled events by exactly the chain's event latency, because a live note cannot be issued early; the pair is refused until a per-track monitor policy defines what the musician hears.

The binding admits an event-to-event chain that ends in exactly one event-to-audio device, up to the admitted chain length; a longer chain, a chain that does not end in the audio-producing device, and a project chain that disagrees with the compiled placement order are all refused because each would bind a node whose prepared latency or routing the compensation shift does not describe.

A retained owned device whose declaration no longer matches the project's authored chain is refused rather than rebound, so a stale node cannot keep playing under a declaration the document has already changed; the caller answers by preparing the binding again from scratch.

Realtime stretch is admitted against declared per-clip and per-program resource limits; a program past those limits is refused at prepare rather than dropped to a lower quality on the audio thread, because a silent quality fallback is indistinguishable from the engine working.

The candidate path re-admits realtime stretch against the same declared limits before a rebind, so a program that grew past them while bound is refused at the same gate rather than reaching the audio thread through an incremental update.

The executor's own topology validation rejected the routed plan; this site relays that verdict with the offending node and index rather than inventing a graph-level reason, and an unmapped validation code falls through to the same refusal so a new executor verdict cannot be admitted by omission.

Creating the track automation renderer failed against its declared lane limits; the binding relays the renderer's own error code and lane id rather than binding a track whose automation would not be delivered.
